h: Deeds Teshuvah and Torah Adorn the Shabbos Bride

p: In the holy Zohar on this parsha
to do with your strength, do' (Koheles 9:10):
this is that a person must
include the left in the right.
as in the expression 'a weak hand'
'Your right hand, Hashem, is glorious in strength,' etc.
'For there is no deed or reckoning
or who is a master of reckoning:
make a reckoning of his deeds
in a place of many lights
with the rest of the tzaddikim,
שֶׁרֵאשִׁית חׇכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קיא, י)
that "the beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" (Tehillim 111:10);
and this is "whatever your hand finds"
which is from the side of Gevurah,
that is, the aspect of ahavah;
and one must include the left in the right,
and this is the aspect of Yaakov Avinu,
And this is the root of the holiness of Shabbos:
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
of the holy Field of Apples,
which is the aspect of Gan Eden,
and it corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu,
and she is included in the attribute of day,
the study of Torah in general;
"to make a reckoning of his deeds";
is the actual performance of the mitzvos.
one merits to delight in Gan Eden,
among the totality of the souls of Yisrael,
as is stated there in the holy Zohar:
will illuminate him in this world
which is a semblance of the World to Come,
And this is alluded to in the words:
alludes to the wisdom of the Torah
the twenty-four adornments of the bride,
through a reckoning of the soul;
alludes to the vessels of the soul,
which is a vessel of fragrance
alludes to the performance of the mitzvos;
the garment of the soul in Gan Eden,
and clothe you in fine garments";
in the name of the holy Rav,
that the garment of the mitzvah
all the souls of Yisrael merit
in the holiness of the day of Shabbos.
For the aspect of performing the mitzvah
resting all the day of Shabbos
that one who sat and did not commit a sin
as one who performs a mitzvah.
which is the reckoning of the soul,
in the holiness of the day of Shabbos,
בְּמִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת (תְּהִלִּים צב, ב)
in "A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos" (Tehillim 92:2):
and it is stated in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 19):
'And one who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy.'"
it is to be made entirely Torah,
and as they, of blessed memory, said
